title: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: A burden can remain unchanged while its public explanation becomes much more attractive.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side examines that recurring social mechanism.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book asks how power makes unpleasant costs appear honorable, necessary, or natural.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Its central question concerns who benefits from the explanation and who carries the load.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The argument travels through history, institutions, emotional life, and artificial intelligence.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: It does not assume that every shared ideal is merely a deliberate deception.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Instead, it follows the relationship between legitimate cooperation and concealed transfers of burden.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: That distinction is the reason to read beyond the title’s provocative image.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The clean side is the account that makes an arrangement acceptable.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: It might speak of duty, harmony, efficiency, expertise, or collective progress.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The dirty thing is the cost that this account can obscure or relocate.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: A person may sincerely believe the explanation while benefiting from its unequal distribution.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Someone else may carry strain without having much influence over the arrangement.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book asks readers to trace both sides of that relationship.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Naming a noble purpose does not settle whether the resulting burden is defensible.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Nor does discovering a burden prove that the purpose has no legitimate value.
